<cell id="cell-3"><cell_type>markdown</cell_type>## The core rule: the vsim measurement window (ROI) is very narrow

This is the single most important limitation. Everything in Tier 1 is a
consequence of it.

When execution hands off to vsim, the resume step writes back only part of
the CPU state. `ResumeDriver::resume` (`resume_driver.hpp`) restores the
GPRs, the FPRs, the V registers, the PC, the privilege level (via
`dcsr.prv`, write-verified), and a fixed set of CSRs: `mstatus`, `mtvec`,
`mscratch`, `mepc`, `mcause`, `mtval`, `mie`, `mip`, `mcycle`, `minstret`,
`fcsr`, and the Andes machine-setup pair `mcache_ctl` / `mmisc_ctl`. An
S/U-privilege handoff also mirrors the PMP block.

It does NOT write `satp`, `medeleg`, or `mideleg` -- S-mode CSRs the M-only
default engine does not implement -- and for an M-mode handoff PMP stays
unrestored (L2, L3, L4). The CSR constants for those names exist in the
driver, but `resume()` never writes them.

The cell below prints every CSR constant the resume driver knows. The list
is deliberately larger than the set it restores: defining a constant (so a
value can be read or drained by number) is not the same as writing it back
into the hart.</cell id="cell-3">

<cell id="cell-5"><cell_type>markdown</cell_type>So the region you measure on vsim (between the entry and exit triggers)
MUST be:

- Single privilege level throughout (M, S, or U -- the real level is
  transported, but the engine RTL must implement it or the resume aborts
  loudly). No privilege CHANGE inside the ROI: that is a trap or an xRET.
- No virtual memory / paging (`satp` stays at its reset = bare mode; L3).
- Trap-free, as the safe contract. The trap CSRs do round-trip and a
  synchronous M-mode trap inside the ROI returns correctly (see L4), but
  delegation and paging-driven faults are still outside the envelope.
- PMP-static for an M-mode handoff (no memory-protection setup is carried
  in; L2).
- No LR/SC reservation held across the boundary (L5).
- No asynchronous interrupts inside the window.
- MMIO limited to the vplat device set -- UART2 + SimControl/HTIF (L9).
  Semihosting via libgloss is not serviced (L1); the vplat runtime's
  MMIO-backed stdio / exit / file io IS.

If the measured region steps outside this envelope, the result is silently
wrong or the run hangs. Each case is below.</cell id="cell-5">
<cell id="cell-6"><cell_type>markdown</cell_type>## State coverage: what the wire format carries

Inventory view of the ROI rule. Checked against `include/hybrid/state_abi.h`
(the struct), the QEMU plugin drain (`qemu_plugin/hybrid_handoff.c`), the
vsim resume (`resume_driver.hpp`), and the vsim drain (`state_drain.hpp`).

### Carried in `hybrid_state_v1`

- 32 GPRs, 32 FPRs
- `fcsr` (frm + sticky fflags), live under `HYBRID_FLAG_FP`
- 13 M-mode CSRs: `mstatus, mepc, mtvec, mcause, mtval, mscratch, medeleg,
  mideleg, mip, mie, mcycle, minstret, satp`
- 2 Andes machine-setup CSRs: `mcache_ctl` (0x7CA), `mmisc_ctl` (0x7D0) --
  the cache / misc enables crt0 writes at boot
- PMP: 16 `pmpcfg` + 64 `pmpaddr`
- V extension: `vstart, vtype, vl, vlenb, vreg[32], vxsat, vxrm, vcsr`
- Warmup metadata: `mcycle_at_measure_start`, `minstret_at_measure_start`
- `reserved[192]` -- room for 24 more `uint64`. (Wire format is version 2;
  L11 widened `vreg[]` to 128 bytes per register.)

### NOT in the wire format at all

- All S-mode CSRs: `stvec, sepc, scause, stval, sscratch, sie, sip,
  scounteren, senvcfg, stimecmp`
- HPM block: `mhpmcounter3..31`, `mhpmevent3..31`, `mcounteren, menvcfg,
  mcountinhibit, mconfigptr, misa, time`
- Every Andes-custom CSR except the cache / misc pair: `mmsc_cfg, micm_cfg,
  mdcm_cfg, mxstatus, mdcause, mnvec`, ... (L21)
- The LR/SC reservation (L5)

### Carried but NOT restored into vsim

The plugin drains these into the struct, but `ResumeDriver` writes none of
them into the hart, so they are dead during an M-mode ROI:

- `satp` (L3), `medeleg`, `mideleg` (L4) -- S-mode CSRs the M-only default
  engine does not implement.
- The PMP block on an M-mode handoff (L2). An S/U handoff DOES mirror it,
  because an S/U access with PMP implemented and no matching entry faults.

The writable M-mode CSRs that DO round-trip -- `mscratch, mepc, mcause,
mtval, mie, mip` alongside `mstatus, mtvec, mcycle, minstret, fcsr` -- are
restored at resume, re-read at drain (`StateDrain::drain_with_passthrough`),
and compared by `--verify`. Two exceptions: `mip` is restored and re-read
but NOT compared (its pending bits are hardware-driven and diverge between
the engines' clocks), and `mtvec` is restored but not re-drained.

### Transport ceiling - why "all CSRs" is not free

Three surfaces, three ceilings:

| Surface         | Mechanism                                     | Ceiling |
|-----------------|-----------------------------------------------|---------|
| QEMU1 drain     | plugin reads by NAME from gdbstub XML         | only CSRs the QEMU fork advertises |
| vsim resume     | DMI Abstract Cmd + Program Buffer (by number) | RO / WARL / locked bits will not take arbitrary values |
| vsim drain      | DMI Abstract read (by number)                 | general for any readable CSR |

Two structural blockers to "all CSRs":

1. The wire format is a fixed C struct; `reserved[192]` fits about 24 more
   `uint64`. Reaching the full M + S + HPM + Andes set needs a v2 layout.
2. Semantics, not just bits. Restore order and side effects already bite
   (`mstatus.FS/VS` gating, `vsetvl` atomicity for `vtype/vl`). Writing
   `satp` flushes the TLB; Andes `mcache_ctl / mmisc_ctl` toggle caches,
   prefetchers and branch prediction -- exactly the CSRs that shape the cycle
   figure, which is why the cache pair is transported (L21).

Verdict: extending the wire format to a bounded set is feasible -- the
`fcsr` work (L20) is the worked example: one `uint64` carved from
`reserved[]`, drained by name, restored via the existing abstract-or-PB
write, read back at drain. S-mode trap CSRs and a chosen Andes microarch
subset can follow the same recipe. "All RISC-V CSRs including Andes-specific"
is not feasible without redesigning the wire format and lifting the entire
ROI envelope (L2-L5).</cell id="cell-6">
<cell id="cell-7"><cell_type>markdown</cell_type>## Tier 1 - Will break on the next real workload

### L2. PMP protection is not carried into vsim for M-mode handoffs  (F-T1.3)

- When it bites: an M-mode workload that relies on PMP-enforced regions
  (write-protect, execute-lock, locked entries) inside the ROI.
- What happens: the plugin drains all 16 `pmpcfg` + 64 `pmpaddr`, but an
  M-mode resume writes none of them back, so vsim runs the ROI with zeroed
  PMP and any phase-1 protection silently disappears. Because M-mode bypasses
  unlocked entries, the usual symptom is the opposite of a fault: an access
  the producer locked down just succeeds.
- S/U handoffs are covered: an S/U resume mirrors the producer's PMP block
  (all 64 `pmpaddr`, then the 8 even `pmpcfg`; tolerant writes), because with
  PMP implemented and no matching entry every S/U access faults -- an S/U ROI
  could not even fetch without it.
- Where: `resume_driver.hpp` -- the PMP mirror is gated on `state.priv != 3`.
- Status: PARTIAL (open for M-mode; locked-entry semantics untested). A clean
  standalone failing fixture needs a locked no-access entry plus a trap
  handler to observe the missing fault, which collides with the trap-free
  envelope, so this one is documented rather than shipped as a `break_*`.</cell id="cell-7">
<cell id="cell-8"><cell_type>markdown</cell_type>### L3. Virtual memory (paging) is off inside the ROI

- When it bites: any workload running with paging enabled (`satp != 0`),
  i.e. almost anything under an OS.
- What happens: `satp` is drained into the state file, but `resume()` never
  writes it. The ROI executes in bare mode, so every virtual address is
  treated as physical and loads/stores hit the wrong memory.
- Where: `resume_driver.hpp` -- `kCsrSatp` (0x180) is defined among the CSR
  constants but `resume()` issues no write for it (it sits in the
  "carried but not restored" set). The default engine is M-only
  (`NDS_NUM_PRIVILEGE_LEVELS=1`), so `satp` is WARL-zero there regardless;
  paging needs an S/U-capable engine first.
- Status: OPEN.</cell id="cell-8">
<cell id="cell-9"><cell_type>markdown</cell_type>### L4. Traps inside the ROI: the CSR data round-trips; delegation and paging faults do not  (F-T1.4)

This entry used to read "trap state is lost across the ROI". That is no
longer true against the code, so it is corrected here.

- What the code does now: the writable trap CSRs `mepc`, `mcause`, `mtval`,
  `mie`, `mip` are restored at resume (`ResumeDriver::resume`,
  `write_csr_tolerant`) and re-read at drain
  (`StateDrain::drain_with_passthrough`), and `mtvec` is restored, so a
  handler installed before the ROI is reachable. A synchronous M-mode trap
  taken inside the ROI returns correctly -- confirmed by running an `ecall`
  whose handler bumps `mepc` and `mret`s through `--model hybrid`: the run
  completes and reports a normal `window_cycles`. The lock-step DV fixture
  `tests/fixtures/rt_trap_ecall.S` exercises the same trap path on the
  co-sim leg.
- What is still open: `medeleg` / `mideleg` are NOT restored, so a trap that
  should delegate to S-mode does not on an S/U engine; with paging off (L3) a
  page-fault path cannot be set up at all; and asynchronous interrupts are
  out of envelope. So the safe contract stays "trap-free", but the failure
  mode is no longer "trap state is silently lost" -- the trap CSR values do
  round-trip and compare under `--verify`.
- Where: `resume_driver.hpp` (restores mepc/mcause/mtval/mie/mip + mtvec;
  medeleg/mideleg/satp deliberately absent),
  `state_drain.hpp::drain_with_passthrough` (re-reads the five).
- Status: PARTIAL. Trap-CSR data round-trips; delegation + paging faults
  open.</cell id="cell-9">
<cell id="cell-10"><cell_type>markdown</cell_type>### L5. An LR/SC reservation cannot cross the handoff  (F-T1.5)

- When it bites: an `lr.{w,d}` retires before the trigger and the matching
  `sc.{w,d}` retires after it -- or any reservation held across the boundary.
- What happens: the reservation is microarchitectural state, absent from the
  wire format (`include/hybrid/state_abi.h` has no reservation field), so it
  never round-trips. vsim resumes with no live reservation, the `sc` always
  fails, and a `__atomic_compare_exchange` loop spins forever.
- Where: `include/hybrid/state_abi.h` (no reservation field); `resume()`
  restores no reservation.
- Status: OPEN. The plan is to reject (not transport) a pending reservation
  at the trigger.

The cell below proves it. `break_lrsc.S` acquires a reservation with `lr.d`
on the QEMU1 leg, crosses the ENTER marker, and runs `sc.d` on the vsim leg.
Standalone (one engine, no handoff) the reservation survives and the program
exits 0; through `--model hybrid` the reservation is lost, the `sc` fails,
and the program spins until the run is killed (bounded here by an outer
`timeout` so the cell returns instead of waiting out the driver's 90 s
guard).</cell id="cell-10">

<cell id="cell-12"><cell_type>markdown</cell_type>## Tier 2 - Will break when you scale up

### L7. No check that the workload fits guest RAM at runtime; overflow corrupts silently  (F-T2.2)

- 128 MB is only the DEFAULT, not the limit. `--mem-size` sets the program
  RAM up to 2 GiB - 4 KiB; the driver maps that PLUS one 4 KiB V-transport
  scratch page on top (L26), so mmap = QEMU memory backend = vsim RAM window.
- When it bites: heap, stack, or static data extends past the size in effect,
  or the workload needs more than 2 GiB at all.
- What happens: the STATIC image is checked -- a load-time guard
  (`elf_load_top` + `cmd_run.cpp`) rejects an ELF whose `PT_LOAD` segments
  reach past `--mem-size` (into the reserved scratch page) with a clear
  "raise --mem-size" message. But RUNTIME growth (heap or stack past the
  ceiling) still has no startup check: vsim's memory rejects or truncates the
  access, QEMU may treat it as MMIO, and nothing names `--mem-size` as the
  cause. Separately, 2 GiB is a hard wall: the AE350 DRAM window is
  `0x00000000..0x80000000`, QEMU rejects a larger `ram_size`, and the driver
  pre-caps `--mem-size` at 2 GiB - 4 KiB.
- Where: `driver/cmd_run.cpp` (128 MB default, the 2 GiB pre-cap, and the
  `elf_load_top` static-image guard, via `driver/elf_syms.hpp`);
  `QEMU/hw/riscv/andes_ae350.c` (DRAM window + ram_size check).
- Status: PARTIAL. The static `PT_LOAD` fit check landed and the V scratch
  can no longer be clobbered (L26); runtime heap/stack overflow past the
  ceiling still corrupts silently. Workaround: pass `--mem-size` large enough
  by hand (USER_GUIDE 2.5); > 2 GiB workloads cannot run.</cell id="cell-12">
<cell id="cell-13"><cell_type>markdown</cell_type>### L8. Single hart only  (F-T2.3)

- When it bites: any multi-hart config (`_NDS_NHART=2`), IPIs, hart-to-hart
  sync.
- What happens: the resume/drain code only handles hart 0. The icount counter
  is a single `uint64_t` (`icount_trigger.hpp`, "Multi-hart out of scope --
  the counter is a single uint64_t"); BBV emit is single-hart
  (`qemu_plugin/bbv_emit.h`, "Single-hart only"). Resuming hart 1 from hart 0
  state corrupts both.
- Where: `resume_driver.hpp`, `state_drain.hpp`, `icount_trigger.hpp`,
  `qemu_plugin/bbv_emit.h`.
- Status: OPEN.</cell id="cell-13">
<cell id="cell-14"><cell_type>markdown</cell_type>### L9. MMIO inside the ROI: only the vplat device set is handled  (F-T2.5)

- When it bites: the ROI touches any device OTHER than the vplat set -- PLIC,
  the timer (`mtime`/`mtimecmp`), ROM, or aliased/device memory -- or expects
  device STATE to survive the handoff.
- What happens: UART2 (`0xf0300000`) and SimControl/HTIF (`0xe0080000`) are
  modeled by BOTH engines (QEMU: `hw/misc/andes_sim_control.c` + the ae350
  memmap; vsim: the AE350 RTL platform natively), so vplat stdio / exit /
  file io inside the ROI work and the hybrid leg relays vsim's UART output.
  Any other device range is engine-specific behavior. And no device state
  (UART FIFO contents, pending interrupts, timer compare) crosses the handoff
  -- only RAM is shared; each engine has its own device instances.
- Where: `QEMU/hw/riscv/andes_ae350.c` (SimControl + UART2 memmap);
  `QEMU/hw/misc/andes_sim_control.c`; `runtime/vplat_syscalls.c`.
- Status: PARTIAL -- the vplat device set works; everything else and
  cross-handoff device state are open.</cell id="cell-14">
<cell id="cell-15"><cell_type>markdown</cell_type>## Tier 3 - Configuration and accuracy limits

### L10. Engines are pluggable, but the machine and CPU family stay fixed

- When it bites: any machine other than `andes_ae350`, any CPU outside the
  `andes-ax45mpv` family.
- What happens: engines are drop-in (`andes-sim list engines`, `--engine ID`,
  discovered via `--describe` or a `.json` sidecar), and the QEMU leg's
  `-cpu ...,vlen={vlen}` is filled from the chosen engine's descriptor

<cell id="cell-16"><cell_type>markdown</cell_type>### L14. The SimPoint cycle estimate is an approximation, not a measurement

- When it bites: any `--mode simpoint` / `./hsim.py estimate` run where you
  read the headline `estimated_cycles` as if it were exact.
- What happens: each phase CPI is sampled from a single window of
  `vsim_icount` instructions at the slice boundary
  (`hsim.py`, `_run_simpoint_pipeline`), and the whole-program figure is
  `N_total * weighted_CPI`. Two accuracy gaps:
  1. The microarchitectural state (caches, branch predictor) is cold at each
     window start unless you pass `--vsim-warmup-icount`. Without warmup the
     CPI is biased high.
  2. No error bound or confidence interval is reported. The estimate inherits
     SimPoint's usual phase-approximation error.
- Where: `hsim.py` (`_run_simpoint_pipeline`). SimPoint still runs only on the
  Python golden; the C++ port has not landed.
- Status: by design; mitigate with `--vsim-warmup-icount`.</cell id="cell-16">
<cell id="cell-17"><cell_type>markdown</cell_type>### L21. Andes vendor CSRs are only partially transported

- When it bites: any workload whose behavior or cycle figure depends on
  Andes-specific CSRs OTHER than the cache / misc pair (`mmsc_cfg, micm_cfg,
  mdcm_cfg, mxstatus, mdcause, mnvec, mslideleg`, ...).
- What happens: the machine-setup pair `mcache_ctl` (0x7CA) and `mmisc_ctl`
  (0x7D0) round-trips. crt0 enables the L1 I/D caches via `csrw mcache_ctl`,
  but that write runs on the cache-less functional engine; without carrying
  it the cycle engine resumed with caches at their reset default -- DISABLED
  -- so the whole window ran uncached and the figure inflated severalfold
  (hello `main`->`_exit`: 14707 -> 2871 cycles). All OTHER Andes vendor CSRs
  do not appear in `hybrid_state_v1`; vsim runs the ROI with whatever its
  reset / boot-time values were, so remaining prefetcher / branch-predictor /
  ECC controls can still shape the cycle count -- an accuracy hazard.
- Where: `include/hybrid/state_abi.h` (`mcache_ctl`/`mmisc_ctl` fields, rest
  absent); `qemu_plugin/hybrid_handoff.c` (drains the pair by gdbstub name);
  `resume_driver.hpp` (tolerant restore, `kCsrMcacheCtl` / `kCsrMmiscCtl`).
- Status: PARTIAL. The cycle-shaping cache pair is transported. The remaining
  vendor CSRs await a v2 Andes block labelling each as microarch-only
  (read-only / boot-set) or software-visible (must round-trip).</cell id="cell-17">

<cell id="cell-21"><cell_type>markdown</cell_type>### L22. Lock-step co-sim cannot handle asynchronous interrupts

- When it bites: a `--model cycle --cosim` DV run whose testbench takes a
  timer / software / external interrupt (anything NOT caused by the current
  instruction). Synchronous exceptions (`ecall`, illegal, `mret`) ARE
  supported -- this is only about async interrupts.
- What happens: the QEMU oracle and the RTL DUT run on independent clocks, so
  each takes the same interrupt at a DIFFERENT retired-instruction index.
  Records are aligned by attempt index, so from the interrupt onward every
  record compares handler-vs-mainloop and the diff reports a flood of false
  divergences. Testbenches must be interrupt-free today.
- Where: `cosim_redesign.md` ("Out of scope / hard assumptions"); the
  lock-step path in `driver/cosim_lockstep.cpp`, `driver/run_plan.cpp`.
- Status: OPEN. Designed fix is the opt-in `--cosim-async` mode (features
  F8-F10 in `cosim_redesign.md`, not yet built). Distinct from L4 / the ROI
  envelope, which make the HYBRID measurement window interrupt-free; L22 is
  the lock-step DV path, which otherwise DOES support synchronous traps.</cell id="cell-21">
<cell id="cell-22"><cell_type>markdown</cell_type>### L25. ROI code that reads or writes time-variant CSRs produces engine-dependent results

- The rule: code inside the ROI must treat `mcycle` (0xB00), `minstret`
  (0xB02), `mip` (0x344), and `time` (0xC01) as opaque. No branches,
  arithmetic, or writes on these CSRs inside the ROI.
- Why: QEMU approximates both cycle and instruction counts with a CPI~=1
  model; vsim counts actual RTL pipeline cycles and retires. `mip` pending
  bits (MTIP, MEIP, MSIP) reflect live timer/platform state that differs
  between the functional and cycle-accurate clocks. These values diverge at
  every architectural moment inside the ROI -- by construction, not by bug.
- What happens if the rule is broken:
  - Branch on `mcycle`/`minstret`: the `--verify` oracle (pure QEMU) takes a
    different branch than the hybrid run (vsim); the diff reports a GPR or PC
    mismatch. The plain run passes; only `--verify` exposes it.
  - Write `mcycle` (e.g. `csrw mcycle, zero` to reset a counter): `StateDrain`
    re-reads the reset value at the exit marker; the reported cycle delta is
    near-zero or underflows -- silently wrong.
- Demonstrated by `tests/fixtures/break_mcycle_write.S` (write corrupts the
  delta) and `tests/fixtures/break_verify_diverge.S` (branch diverges under
  `--verify`), run below.
- Distinction from L22: L22 is async interrupts in the lock-step DV path; L25
  is the hybrid measurement path and any code that reads or modifies
  time-variant state inside the ROI.
- Status: by design. A static linter on the ELF could warn on in-ROI
  reads/writes of these CSRs (not built).</cell id="cell-22">

### L1. Semihosting inside the ROI is fatal; vplat is the supported I/O path  (F-T1.1) -- RESOLVED in-tree

libgloss semihosting emits the magic triple (`slli x0,x0,0x1f; ebreak;
srai x0,x0,0x7`); vsim has no semihosting handler, so the ebreak traps, the
trap handler calls `_exit` (another ebreak), and the run loops forever until
it times out. The fix is the vplat runtime
(`build/runtime/libandes_sim_runtime.a`, sources in `runtime/`, link with
`-B build/runtime -specs=andes-sim.specs`): it routes stdio to UART2, exit to
SimControl, and file io to HTIF -- MMIO devices both engines model -- so
`printf` / `exit` / `fopen` inside the ROI work on fast, cycle, AND hybrid
(USER_GUIDE section 5; smoke tests in `tests/vplat/`). Every C fixture in the
repo links it; nothing in-tree uses `-lgloss_vh`. The limitation survives
only for EXTERNAL binaries linked against a semihosting libgloss: keep their
I/O in phase 1 (the QEMU leg, before the ROI), or relink with vplat.

<cell id="cell-29"><cell_type>markdown</cell_type>### L11. VLEN ceiling  (F-T3.4) -- RESOLVED for the supported range 128..1024

Was: the wire format reserved 64 bytes per vector register (VLEN 512) and the
plugin CLAMPED the drained bytes to that with no warning -- a wider engine
silently lost the upper bytes of every V register. Now
`HYBRID_VLEN_BYTES_MAX = 128` (state version 2) covers VLEN 128..1024; the
plugin REFUSES to drain an over-ceiling vlenb (`hybrid_v_drain_policy`)
instead of clamping, vsim's `load_state` rejects an over-ceiling state file
the same way, and every reader rejects version-1 files loudly. The live width
is the runtime `vlenb`, so one struct layout serves every engine and the legs
never disagree on offsets. Verified per VLEN with `tests/fixtures/rt_c_v_fill.c`
(whole-register fill + in-ROI self-check) and `tests/hybrid/e2e_vlen1024_drain.sh`.
Residual (ROADMAP F-ENG-03): a vsim-side compare of the live hart vlenb vs
`state.vlenb` at resume is still open; no built RTL engine reports VLEN 256 or
1024 today, so those widths are validated on the QEMU side.

### L12. CSR 0x7C0 trigger collision -- RESOLVED by the trigger redesign

The old default trigger matched `csrwi 0x7C0, 0/1`, so a real write to that
CSR would false-trigger a handoff. The default trigger is now the marker HINT
pair `slti x0, x0, 0x5A0/0x5A1` -- rd=x0 makes them architectural NOPs, no
CSR is repurposed, and a compiler never emits them on its own (users get them
from `<andes_sim/ROI.h>`). Binaries you cannot edit use `--trigger pc`.
Where: `qemu_plugin/hybrid_handoff.c` (marker matcher);
`verilator/src/hybrid/csr_trigger.hpp`.

### L13. Marker must be a 32-bit instruction  (B18) -- RESOLVED (exact by construction)

The matcher skips any instruction whose size is not 4 bytes, but the markers
are now `slti x0, x0, imm` and SLTI has no compressed form, so the `sz != 4`
skip is exact rather than an approximation (`hybrid_handoff.c`).</cell id="cell-29">

<cell id="cell-31"><cell_type>markdown</cell_type>### L23. mscratch (M-mode software scratch CSR) did not round-trip -- RESOLVED

`mscratch` (CSR 0x340) is the M-mode software scratch register -- a
side-effect-free read/write CSR, legal inside a trap-free, single-privilege
ROI. It was drained by QEMU1 but never restored into vsim and never re-read
at drain, so a value stashed before the ROI read back as the vsim reset value
(the resume gap) and a value written inside the ROI was dropped from the
drained state (the drain gap); `--verify` could not catch the second because
`state_diff` excluded `mscratch` as a "passthrough CSR", and the repo's guard
(`rt_csr_survival.S`) had gone dead in the 2-phase redesign. This broke a
workload sitting ENTIRELY inside the supposedly-safe envelope, so the
envelope list was incomplete. Now `mscratch` round-trips: restored via the
tolerant CSR write right after `mtvec`, re-read in
`drain_with_passthrough`, and strictly compared by `state_diff` in the hybrid
policy. Guard: `rt_csr_survival.S` revived as a live 2-phase self-check, plus
unit cases in `resume_driver.test.cpp` / `state_drain.test.cpp` /
`state_diff_test.cpp`.

### L24. Writable M-mode trap/interrupt CSRs did not round-trip -- RESOLVED

Same shape as L23, for `mepc`, `mcause`, `mtval`, `mie`, `mip` -- writable
M-mode CSRs that read/write without a trap, interrupt, or paging. They were
drained but never restored and never re-read, so they suffered the same
resume gap + drain gap and `--verify` was blind to them. Now
`ResumeDriver::resume` restores all five via tolerant abstract writes,
`StateDrain::drain_with_passthrough` re-reads all five, and `state_diff`
compares `mepc`/`mcause`/`mtval`/`mie` under the hybrid policy
(`mepc`/`mcause` also lock-step). The exception is `mip`: restored and re-read
but EXCLUDED from `--verify`, because its pending bits (MTIP/MEIP/MSIP) are
hardware/platform-driven and the timer bit advances differently in the
functional vs cycle clocks, so comparing it would false-positive. On the
M-only default engine the `mip` restore is a no-op; it does real work on
S-capable engines. `medeleg`/`mideleg`/`satp` stay unrestored (S-mode CSRs the
default engine lacks; see L3/L4). This is what made L4 stop being "trap state
is lost".

### L26. V transport scratch moved above the program's RAM -- RESOLVED

Was: the V-register transport staged 32 vector registers through a FIXED guest
address `0x00FF0000` (15 MiB), INSIDE the program's RAM. On every resume on a
V-capable core (the V flag is set from register ADVERTISEMENT, not use, so even
a program issuing no V instruction triggered it) `ResumeDriver` wrote the
drained V bytes there, silently clobbering any program data at that address.
Now the scratch is the TOP page of the mapped RAM span,
`v_scratch_gpa(ram_base, ram_size) = ram_base + ram_size -
HYBRID_V_SCRATCH_BYTES`; the driver maps one page MORE than `--mem-size`
(`shm.cpp`), so the scratch sits just above the program's declared RAM where
no layout can reach it, and a load-time guard (`elf_load_top` + `cmd_run.cpp`)
rejects an ELF whose static image extends into the reserved page.
`ResumeDriver`/`StateDrain` take the GPA as a required-when-V argument and
throw if it is unset (no silent transport through a bogus address). Users see
nothing change -- they get their full `--mem-size`; the reservation is one
hidden page on top. `break_vscratch.S` (sentinel at the old 0x00FF0000) now
PASSES, and `break_vscratch_top.S` (sentinel at the program's last page)
PASSES, proving the scratch sits above program RAM.</cell id="cell-31">
<cell id="cell-32"><cell_type>markdown</cell_type>## Commercial product quality rating

Honest scorecard for "is this a shippable commercial product today?". Rated
against industry baselines (Synopsys VCS, Cadence Xcelium, gem5 + functional
warmup) for a CPU vendor's hybrid-sim offering.

**Overall: 4/10 as a shippable commercial product. ~7/10 as an internal /
research tool inside its narrow design envelope.**

### Axis breakdown

| Axis                                  | Score | Note |
|---------------------------------------|-------|------|
| Architecture clarity                  | 8/10  | Two-phase handoff is clean; shared ABI is a single header. |
| Engineering discipline                | 7/10  | TDD gate, doctest, parallel CI, a candid limitations doc. |
| State coverage (correctness surface)  | 4/10  | 26 documented limitations (11 resolved/removed); 13 scalar CSRs round-trip into vsim, plus privilege, the V CSRs, and PMP for S/U. |
| Generality of workload                | 2/10  | ROI must be single-privilege (M/S/U), effectively trap-free, paging-off (L2-L5). |
| ISA completeness                      | 3/10  | S/U mode and fcsr now transport; still no HPM, zero Andes vendor CSRs beyond the cache/misc pair (vendor IS Andes). |
| Wire-format extensibility             | 4/10  | v1 only; growth happens by carving `reserved[192]` ad-hoc. No v2 path. |
| Robustness / errors                   | 5/10  | `cmderr` is cleared and swallowed; only a private diagnostic side channel. |
| Docs / onboarding                     | 7/10  | `CLAUDE.md`, `USER_GUIDE.md`, and this notebook are unusually honest. |
| Test fixtures                         | 6/10  | Solid asm + C-runtime e2e; FP-rounding and S/U-privilege covered; LR/SC and time-variant-CSR break fixtures; still no in-ROI trap-fault fixture. |
| Portability                           | 4/10  | x86-64 host + little-endian assumed (L18); pinned Andes toolchain; podman-only vsim build. |

### What blocks commercial shipping

1. **Silent correctness gaps.** `cmderr` is W1C-cleared, so a partial CSR
   restore is observable only through a private counter
   (`resume_driver.hpp`, `cmderr_clear_count()`).
2. **ROI envelope is too narrow.** S/U privilege transports now (on an
   S/U-capable engine), but "no paging, no delegation, effectively no traps,
   no semihosting inside the window" (L2-L5) still rules out every real
   OS-bearing benchmark -- SPEC under Linux, any driver code, anything with
   page faults. The vplat runtime covers bare-metal I/O only.
3. **No Andes vendor CSRs beyond the cache/misc pair.** For an Andes product,
   shipping near-zero `mmsc_cfg / mxstatus / ...` transport (L21) is a
   credibility hit and an accuracy hazard -- prefetcher and predictor controls
   shape the cycle count.
4. **13 scalar CSRs restored into vsim** (`mstatus, mtvec, mscratch, mepc,
   mcause, mtval, mie, mip, mcycle, minstret, fcsr, mcache_ctl, mmisc_ctl`),
   plus `dcsr.prv` and -- for S/U handoffs -- the PMP block. `satp` and
   `medeleg`/`mideleg` (and PMP on M-mode handoffs) are drained but never
   written back. Any future need for paging or S-mode delegation inside the
   ROI needs `resume_driver` extended.
5. **Wire format is v1-locked with ad-hoc growth.** Each new field steals
   from `reserved[]` (warmup metadata, fcsr, the cache pair). No deprecation
   path, no feature bits beyond the three `HYBRID_FLAG_*` bits.
6. **Build/test infrastructure is single-host.** Podman-required vsim build,
   a practical `JOBS=8` ceiling on 128-core hosts, `/dev/shm`-backed fixtures
   -- fine for a lab, painful for a commercial CI matrix.

### What it does well (the 7/10 internal-tool score)

- Two-phase handoff is a clear, documented contract.
- `state_abi.h` plus `static_assert`s pin layout -- good ABI hygiene.
- The team writes down what does NOT work (this notebook) instead of hiding
  it. Commercially that is the release-blocker checklist; internally it is
  exemplary.
- SimPoint integration for whole-program cycle estimation (L14) is a real
  differentiator over a pure functional sim.

### Bottom line

Ship-grade architecture, research-grade coverage. For commercial release you
need: a v2 wire format with feature bits and a deprecation path; paging +
delegation supported inside the ROI (close L3, L4); Andes vendor CSR transport
(close L21); a proper error policy instead of `cmderr` swallowing; and the
existing `--verify`/`--cosim` oracle (L15) extended to icount/simpoint and
wired into CI. Rough effort: 6-9 months of focused hardening, not weeks.</cell id="cell-32">

## The core rule: the vsim measurement window (ROI) is very narrow

This is the single most important limitation. Everything in Tier 1 is a
consequence of it.

When execution hands off to vsim, the resume step writes back only part of
the CPU state. `ResumeDriver::resume` (`resume_driver.hpp`) restores the
GPRs, the FPRs, the V registers, the PC, the privilege level (via
`dcsr.prv`, write-verified), and a fixed set of CSRs: `mstatus`, `mtvec`,
`mscratch`, `mepc`, `mcause`, `mtval`, `mie`, `mip`, `mcycle`, `minstret`,
`fcsr`, and the Andes machine-setup pair `mcache_ctl` / `mmisc_ctl`. An
S/U-privilege handoff also mirrors the PMP block.

It does NOT write `satp`, `medeleg`, or `mideleg` -- S-mode CSRs the M-only
default engine does not implement -- and for an M-mode handoff PMP stays
unrestored (L2, L3, L4). The CSR constants for those names exist in the
driver, but `resume()` never writes them.

The cell below prints every CSR constant the resume driver knows. The list
is deliberately larger than the set it restores: defining a constant (so a
value can be read or drained by number) is not the same as writing it back
into the hart.
!grep -n "static constexpr uint16_t kCsr" verilator/src/hybrid/resume_driver.hpp

So the region you measure on vsim (between the entry and exit triggers)
MUST be:

- Single privilege level throughout (M, S, or U -- the real level is
  transported, but the engine RTL must implement it or the resume aborts
  loudly). No privilege CHANGE inside the ROI: that is a trap or an xRET.
- No virtual memory / paging (`satp` stays at its reset = bare mode; L3).
- Trap-free, as the safe contract. The trap CSRs do round-trip and a
  synchronous M-mode trap inside the ROI returns correctly (see L4), but
  delegation and paging-driven faults are still outside the envelope.
- PMP-static for an M-mode handoff (no memory-protection setup is carried
  in; L2).
- No LR/SC reservation held across the boundary (L5).
- No asynchronous interrupts inside the window.
- MMIO limited to the vplat device set -- UART2 + SimControl/HTIF (L9).
  Semihosting via libgloss is not serviced (L1); the vplat runtime's
  MMIO-backed stdio / exit / file io IS.

If the measured region steps outside this envelope, the result is silently
wrong or the run hangs. Each case is below.

## State coverage: what the wire format carries

Inventory view of the ROI rule. Checked against `include/hybrid/state_abi.h`
(the struct), the QEMU plugin drain (`qemu_plugin/hybrid_handoff.c`), the
vsim resume (`resume_driver.hpp`), and the vsim drain (`state_drain.hpp`).

### Carried in `hybrid_state_v1`

- 32 GPRs, 32 FPRs
- `fcsr` (frm + sticky fflags), live under `HYBRID_FLAG_FP`
- 13 M-mode CSRs: `mstatus, mepc, mtvec, mcause, mtval, mscratch, medeleg,
  mideleg, mip, mie, mcycle, minstret, satp`
- 2 Andes machine-setup CSRs: `mcache_ctl` (0x7CA), `mmisc_ctl` (0x7D0) --
  the cache / misc enables crt0 writes at boot
- PMP: 16 `pmpcfg` + 64 `pmpaddr`
- V extension: `vstart, vtype, vl, vlenb, vreg[32], vxsat, vxrm, vcsr`
- Warmup metadata: `mcycle_at_measure_start`, `minstret_at_measure_start`
- `reserved[192]` -- room for 24 more `uint64`. (Wire format is version 2;
  L11 widened `vreg[]` to 128 bytes per register.)

### NOT in the wire format at all

- All S-mode CSRs: `stvec, sepc, scause, stval, sscratch, sie, sip,
  scounteren, senvcfg, stimecmp`
- HPM block: `mhpmcounter3..31`, `mhpmevent3..31`, `mcounteren, menvcfg,
  mcountinhibit, mconfigptr, misa, time`
- Every Andes-custom CSR except the cache / misc pair: `mmsc_cfg, micm_cfg,
  mdcm_cfg, mxstatus, mdcause, mnvec`, ... (L21)
- The LR/SC reservation (L5)

### Carried but NOT restored into vsim

The plugin drains these into the struct, but `ResumeDriver` writes none of
them into the hart, so they are dead during an M-mode ROI:

- `satp` (L3), `medeleg`, `mideleg` (L4) -- S-mode CSRs the M-only default
  engine does not implement.
- The PMP block on an M-mode handoff (L2). An S/U handoff DOES mirror it,
  because an S/U access with PMP implemented and no matching entry faults.

The writable M-mode CSRs that DO round-trip -- `mscratch, mepc, mcause,
mtval, mie, mip` alongside `mstatus, mtvec, mcycle, minstret, fcsr` -- are
restored at resume, re-read at drain (`StateDrain::drain_with_passthrough`),
and compared by `--verify`. Two exceptions: `mip` is restored and re-read
but NOT compared (its pending bits are hardware-driven and diverge between
the engines' clocks), and `mtvec` is restored but not re-drained.

### Transport ceiling - why "all CSRs" is not free

Three surfaces, three ceilings:

| Surface         | Mechanism                                     | Ceiling |
|-----------------|-----------------------------------------------|---------|
| QEMU1 drain     | plugin reads by NAME from gdbstub XML         | only CSRs the QEMU fork advertises |
| vsim resume     | DMI Abstract Cmd + Program Buffer (by number) | RO / WARL / locked bits will not take arbitrary values |
| vsim drain      | DMI Abstract read (by number)                 | general for any readable CSR |

Two structural blockers to "all CSRs":

1. The wire format is a fixed C struct; `reserved[192]` fits about 24 more
   `uint64`. Reaching the full M + S + HPM + Andes set needs a v2 layout.
2. Semantics, not just bits. Restore order and side effects already bite
   (`mstatus.FS/VS` gating, `vsetvl` atomicity for `vtype/vl`). Writing
   `satp` flushes the TLB; Andes `mcache_ctl / mmisc_ctl` toggle caches,
   prefetchers and branch prediction -- exactly the CSRs that shape the cycle
   figure, which is why the cache pair is transported (L21).

Verdict: extending the wire format to a bounded set is feasible -- the
`fcsr` work (L20) is the worked example: one `uint64` carved from
`reserved[]`, drained by name, restored via the existing abstract-or-PB
write, read back at drain. S-mode trap CSRs and a chosen Andes microarch
subset can follow the same recipe. "All RISC-V CSRs including Andes-specific"
is not feasible without redesigning the wire format and lifting the entire
ROI envelope (L2-L5).

## Tier 1 - Will break on the next real workload

### L2. PMP protection is not carried into vsim for M-mode handoffs  (F-T1.3)

- When it bites: an M-mode workload that relies on PMP-enforced regions
  (write-protect, execute-lock, locked entries) inside the ROI.
- What happens: the plugin drains all 16 `pmpcfg` + 64 `pmpaddr`, but an
  M-mode resume writes none of them back, so vsim runs the ROI with zeroed
  PMP and any phase-1 protection silently disappears. Because M-mode bypasses
  unlocked entries, the usual symptom is the opposite of a fault: an access
  the producer locked down just succeeds.
- S/U handoffs are covered: an S/U resume mirrors the producer's PMP block
  (all 64 `pmpaddr`, then the 8 even `pmpcfg`; tolerant writes), because with
  PMP implemented and no matching entry every S/U access faults -- an S/U ROI
  could not even fetch without it.
- Where: `resume_driver.hpp` -- the PMP mirror is gated on `state.priv != 3`.
- Status: PARTIAL (open for M-mode; locked-entry semantics untested). A clean
  standalone failing fixture needs a locked no-access entry plus a trap
  handler to observe the missing fault, which collides with the trap-free
  envelope, so this one is documented rather than shipped as a `break_*`.

### L3. Virtual memory (paging) is off inside the ROI

- When it bites: any workload running with paging enabled (`satp != 0`),
  i.e. almost anything under an OS.
- What happens: `satp` is drained into the state file, but `resume()` never
  writes it. The ROI executes in bare mode, so every virtual address is
  treated as physical and loads/stores hit the wrong memory.
- Where: `resume_driver.hpp` -- `kCsrSatp` (0x180) is defined among the CSR
  constants but `resume()` issues no write for it (it sits in the
  "carried but not restored" set). The default engine is M-only
  (`NDS_NUM_PRIVILEGE_LEVELS=1`), so `satp` is WARL-zero there regardless;
  paging needs an S/U-capable engine first.
- Status: OPEN.

### L4. Traps inside the ROI: the CSR data round-trips; delegation and paging faults do not  (F-T1.4)

This entry used to read "trap state is lost across the ROI". That is no
longer true against the code, so it is corrected here.

- What the code does now: the writable trap CSRs `mepc`, `mcause`, `mtval`,
  `mie`, `mip` are restored at resume (`ResumeDriver::resume`,
  `write_csr_tolerant`) and re-read at drain
  (`StateDrain::drain_with_passthrough`), and `mtvec` is restored, so a
  handler installed before the ROI is reachable. A synchronous M-mode trap
  taken inside the ROI returns correctly -- confirmed by running an `ecall`
  whose handler bumps `mepc` and `mret`s through `--model hybrid`: the run
  completes and reports a normal `window_cycles`. The lock-step DV fixture
  `tests/fixtures/rt_trap_ecall.S` exercises the same trap path on the
  co-sim leg.
- What is still open: `medeleg` / `mideleg` are NOT restored, so a trap that
  should delegate to S-mode does not on an S/U engine; with paging off (L3) a
  page-fault path cannot be set up at all; and asynchronous interrupts are
  out of envelope. So the safe contract stays "trap-free", but the failure
  mode is no longer "trap state is silently lost" -- the trap CSR values do
  round-trip and compare under `--verify`.
- Where: `resume_driver.hpp` (restores mepc/mcause/mtval/mie/mip + mtvec;
  medeleg/mideleg/satp deliberately absent),
  `state_drain.hpp::drain_with_passthrough` (re-reads the five).
- Status: PARTIAL. Trap-CSR data round-trips; delegation + paging faults
  open.

### L5. An LR/SC reservation cannot cross the handoff  (F-T1.5)

- When it bites: an `lr.{w,d}` retires before the trigger and the matching
  `sc.{w,d}` retires after it -- or any reservation held across the boundary.
- What happens: the reservation is microarchitectural state, absent from the
  wire format (`include/hybrid/state_abi.h` has no reservation field), so it
  never round-trips. vsim resumes with no live reservation, the `sc` always
  fails, and a `__atomic_compare_exchange` loop spins forever.
- Where: `include/hybrid/state_abi.h` (no reservation field); `resume()`
  restores no reservation.
- Status: OPEN. The plan is to reject (not transport) a pending reservation
  at the trigger.

The cell below proves it. `break_lrsc.S` acquires a reservation with `lr.d`
on the QEMU1 leg, crosses the ENTER marker, and runs `sc.d` on the vsim leg.
Standalone (one engine, no handoff) the reservation survives and the program
exits 0; through `--model hybrid` the reservation is lost, the `sc` fails,
and the program spins until the run is killed (bounded here by an outer
`timeout` so the cell returns instead of waiting out the driver's 90 s
guard).

# Standalone fast (no handoff): reservation survives, sc succeeds, exit 0.
!andes-sim run --model fast tests/fixtures/break_lrsc.elf \
    && echo "[standalone fast] PASS: sc succeeded (reservation survived)"

# Hybrid: lr.d retires on QEMU1, sc.d on vsim with no reservation -> sc fails
# -> the program spins. The non-zero exit / kill IS the limitation.
!timeout 30 andes-sim run --model hybrid --trigger marker \
    --engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium tests/fixtures/break_lrsc.elf ; \
 echo "[hybrid] exit $? (124 = killed = the documented hang: reservation lost)"

[hsim mmap] 128.0 MiB at /dev/shm (free: 251.5 GiB)
[hybrid] exit 124 (124 = killed = the documented hang: reservation lost)

## Tier 2 - Will break when you scale up

### L7. No check that the workload fits guest RAM at runtime; overflow corrupts silently  (F-T2.2)

- 128 MB is only the DEFAULT, not the limit. `--mem-size` sets the program
  RAM up to 2 GiB - 4 KiB; the driver maps that PLUS one 4 KiB V-transport
  scratch page on top (L26), so mmap = QEMU memory backend = vsim RAM window.
- When it bites: heap, stack, or static data extends past the size in effect,
  or the workload needs more than 2 GiB at all.
- What happens: the STATIC image is checked -- a load-time guard
  (`elf_load_top` + `cmd_run.cpp`) rejects an ELF whose `PT_LOAD` segments
  reach past `--mem-size` (into the reserved scratch page) with a clear
  "raise --mem-size" message. But RUNTIME growth (heap or stack past the
  ceiling) still has no startup check: vsim's memory rejects or truncates the
  access, QEMU may treat it as MMIO, and nothing names `--mem-size` as the
  cause. Separately, 2 GiB is a hard wall: the AE350 DRAM window is
  `0x00000000..0x80000000`, QEMU rejects a larger `ram_size`, and the driver
  pre-caps `--mem-size` at 2 GiB - 4 KiB.
- Where: `driver/cmd_run.cpp` (128 MB default, the 2 GiB pre-cap, and the
  `elf_load_top` static-image guard, via `driver/elf_syms.hpp`);
  `QEMU/hw/riscv/andes_ae350.c` (DRAM window + ram_size check).
- Status: PARTIAL. The static `PT_LOAD` fit check landed and the V scratch
  can no longer be clobbered (L26); runtime heap/stack overflow past the
  ceiling still corrupts silently. Workaround: pass `--mem-size` large enough
  by hand (USER_GUIDE 2.5); > 2 GiB workloads cannot run.

### L8. Single hart only  (F-T2.3)

- When it bites: any multi-hart config (`_NDS_NHART=2`), IPIs, hart-to-hart
  sync.
- What happens: the resume/drain code only handles hart 0. The icount counter
  is a single `uint64_t` (`icount_trigger.hpp`, "Multi-hart out of scope --
  the counter is a single uint64_t"); BBV emit is single-hart
  (`qemu_plugin/bbv_emit.h`, "Single-hart only"). Resuming hart 1 from hart 0
  state corrupts both.
- Where: `resume_driver.hpp`, `state_drain.hpp`, `icount_trigger.hpp`,
  `qemu_plugin/bbv_emit.h`.
- Status: OPEN.

### L9. MMIO inside the ROI: only the vplat device set is handled  (F-T2.5)

- When it bites: the ROI touches any device OTHER than the vplat set -- PLIC,
  the timer (`mtime`/`mtimecmp`), ROM, or aliased/device memory -- or expects
  device STATE to survive the handoff.
- What happens: UART2 (`0xf0300000`) and SimControl/HTIF (`0xe0080000`) are
  modeled by BOTH engines (QEMU: `hw/misc/andes_sim_control.c` + the ae350
  memmap; vsim: the AE350 RTL platform natively), so vplat stdio / exit /
  file io inside the ROI work and the hybrid leg relays vsim's UART output.
  Any other device range is engine-specific behavior. And no device state
  (UART FIFO contents, pending interrupts, timer compare) crosses the handoff
  -- only RAM is shared; each engine has its own device instances.
- Where: `QEMU/hw/riscv/andes_ae350.c` (SimControl + UART2 memmap);
  `QEMU/hw/misc/andes_sim_control.c`; `runtime/vplat_syscalls.c`.
- Status: PARTIAL -- the vplat device set works; everything else and
  cross-handoff device state are open.

## Tier 3 - Configuration and accuracy limits

### L10. Engines are pluggable, but the machine and CPU family stay fixed

- When it bites: any machine other than `andes_ae350`, any CPU outside the
  `andes-ax45mpv` family.
- What happens: engines are drop-in (`andes-sim list engines`, `--engine ID`,
  discovered via `--describe` or a `.json` sidecar), and the QEMU leg's
  `-cpu ...,vlen={vlen}` is filled from the chosen engine's descriptor
  (`driver/engine_registry.cpp`). But `-machine andes_ae350` and the
  `andes-ax45mpv` CPU name are still literals there. The V-register scratch
  address is NO LONGER a fixed constant -- it is the mmap's top page
  (`v_scratch_gpa(ram_base, ram_size)`, L26), derived from the runtime RAM
  base + size, so it adapts to any base and is no longer a porting blocker.
- Where: `driver/engine_registry.cpp`.
- Status: PARTIAL -- engine variant + VLEN are pluggable and the scratch GPA
  is runtime-derived; the machine and CPU family are still literals that
  block porting to another core.

### L14. The SimPoint cycle estimate is an approximation, not a measurement

- When it bites: any `--mode simpoint` / `./hsim.py estimate` run where you
  read the headline `estimated_cycles` as if it were exact.
- What happens: each phase CPI is sampled from a single window of
  `vsim_icount` instructions at the slice boundary
  (`hsim.py`, `_run_simpoint_pipeline`), and the whole-program figure is
  `N_total * weighted_CPI`. Two accuracy gaps:
  1. The microarchitectural state (caches, branch predictor) is cold at each
     window start unless you pass `--vsim-warmup-icount`. Without warmup the
     CPI is biased high.
  2. No error bound or confidence interval is reported. The estimate inherits
     SimPoint's usual phase-approximation error.
- Where: `hsim.py` (`_run_simpoint_pipeline`). SimPoint still runs only on the
  Python golden; the C++ port has not landed.
- Status: by design; mitigate with `--vsim-warmup-icount`.

### L21. Andes vendor CSRs are only partially transported

- When it bites: any workload whose behavior or cycle figure depends on
  Andes-specific CSRs OTHER than the cache / misc pair (`mmsc_cfg, micm_cfg,
  mdcm_cfg, mxstatus, mdcause, mnvec, mslideleg`, ...).
- What happens: the machine-setup pair `mcache_ctl` (0x7CA) and `mmisc_ctl`
  (0x7D0) round-trips. crt0 enables the L1 I/D caches via `csrw mcache_ctl`,
  but that write runs on the cache-less functional engine; without carrying
  it the cycle engine resumed with caches at their reset default -- DISABLED
  -- so the whole window ran uncached and the figure inflated severalfold
  (hello `main`->`_exit`: 14707 -> 2871 cycles). All OTHER Andes vendor CSRs
  do not appear in `hybrid_state_v1`; vsim runs the ROI with whatever its
  reset / boot-time values were, so remaining prefetcher / branch-predictor /
  ECC controls can still shape the cycle count -- an accuracy hazard.
- Where: `include/hybrid/state_abi.h` (`mcache_ctl`/`mmisc_ctl` fields, rest
  absent); `qemu_plugin/hybrid_handoff.c` (drains the pair by gdbstub name);
  `resume_driver.hpp` (tolerant restore, `kCsrMcacheCtl` / `kCsrMmiscCtl`).
- Status: PARTIAL. The cycle-shaping cache pair is transported. The remaining
  vendor CSRs await a v2 Andes block labelling each as microarch-only
  (read-only / boot-set) or software-visible (must round-trip).

## Tier 4 - Robustness and tooling gaps

### L15. Value-level handoff check: shipped for marker/pc, missing for icount/simpoint  (F-T3.1)

- When it bites: any bug that copies the wrong register, byte-swaps, or
  truncates a 64-bit value in the icount or simpoint paths.
- What happens: `run --verify` (marker/pc only, dev tier) re-runs the ELF on a
  pure-QEMU oracle and diffs the FULL drained state field by field;
  `--cosim [--cosim-interval N]` goes further and localizes a divergence to
  the first bad N-retire window (it suppresses the cycle figure -- the
  checkpoint drains pollute it; rerun without `--cosim` to measure). Both are
  manual, not CI-wired. The icount trigger and the SimPoint pipeline still
  assert only exit code and PC range -- a wrong register value there passes
  silently.
- Where: `driver/cmd_run.cpp` (the `--verify` oracle path and `state_diff`);
  `hsim.py` (`_run_drain_pair`, `_run_simpoint_pipeline`) -- unchecked.
- Status: PARTIAL -- marker/pc covered by `--verify`/`--cosim`; icount +
  simpoint coverage and CI wiring still open.

### L18. Wire format is little-endian / same-arch only

- When it bites: running any component on a big-endian host, or mixing hosts
  with different struct alignment.
- What happens: the state struct is exchanged byte-for-byte with no byte-swap
  path (`state_abi.h`, the endianness note). The Python mirror (golden only)
  uses a native-endian `ctypes.Structure` (`abi.py`), so a BE host would
  mis-parse the body while the magic check still passes -- a silent mis-read.
- Where: `include/hybrid/state_abi.h` (endianness note); `abi.py`.
- Status: by design (x86-64 host + RV64 guest only).

### L19. Other un-guarded failure paths  (F-T3.3, F-T3.5, F-T3.6, F-T3.8)

- Determinism is not guaranteed across re-runs (reserved bytes, CSR drain
  order); no test pins byte-identical output.
- Submodule version drift (QEMU plugin ABI, vsim DM, pinned SimPoint
  `17783e5`) has no CI gate.
- Failure injection is thin: partial drain, disk full, mmap truncated mid-run
  are not covered.
- Status: all OPEN, lower priority.

### L22. Lock-step co-sim cannot handle asynchronous interrupts

- When it bites: a `--model cycle --cosim` DV run whose testbench takes a
  timer / software / external interrupt (anything NOT caused by the current
  instruction). Synchronous exceptions (`ecall`, illegal, `mret`) ARE
  supported -- this is only about async interrupts.
- What happens: the QEMU oracle and the RTL DUT run on independent clocks, so
  each takes the same interrupt at a DIFFERENT retired-instruction index.
  Records are aligned by attempt index, so from the interrupt onward every
  record compares handler-vs-mainloop and the diff reports a flood of false
  divergences. Testbenches must be interrupt-free today.
- Where: `cosim_redesign.md` ("Out of scope / hard assumptions"); the
  lock-step path in `driver/cosim_lockstep.cpp`, `driver/run_plan.cpp`.
- Status: OPEN. Designed fix is the opt-in `--cosim-async` mode (features

### L25. ROI code that reads or writes time-variant CSRs produces engine-dependent results

- The rule: code inside the ROI must treat `mcycle` (0xB00), `minstret`
  (0xB02), `mip` (0x344), and `time` (0xC01) as opaque. No branches,
  arithmetic, or writes on these CSRs inside the ROI.
- Why: QEMU approximates both cycle and instruction counts with a CPI~=1
  model; vsim counts actual RTL pipeline cycles and retires. `mip` pending
  bits (MTIP, MEIP, MSIP) reflect live timer/platform state that differs
  between the functional and cycle-accurate clocks. These values diverge at
  every architectural moment inside the ROI -- by construction, not by bug.
- What happens if the rule is broken:
  - Branch on `mcycle`/`minstret`: the `--verify` oracle (pure QEMU) takes a
    different branch than the hybrid run (vsim); the diff reports a GPR or PC
    mismatch. The plain run passes; only `--verify` exposes it.
  - Write `mcycle` (e.g. `csrw mcycle, zero` to reset a counter): `StateDrain`
    re-reads the reset value at the exit marker; the reported cycle delta is
    near-zero or underflows -- silently wrong.
- Demonstrated by `tests/fixtures/break_mcycle_write.S` (write corrupts the
  delta) and `tests/fixtures/break_verify_diverge.S` (branch diverges under
  `--verify`), run below.
- Distinction from L22: L22 is async interrupts in the lock-step DV path; L25
  is the hybrid measurement path and any code that reads or modifies
  time-variant state inside the ROI.
- Status: by design. A static linter on the ELF could warn on in-ROI
  reads/writes of these CSRs (not built).

### L1. Semihosting inside the ROI is fatal; vplat is the supported I/O path  (F-T1.1) -- RESOLVED in-tree

libgloss semihosting emits the magic triple (`slli x0,x0,0x1f; ebreak;
srai x0,x0,0x7`); vsim has no semihosting handler, so the ebreak traps, the
trap handler calls `_exit` (another ebreak), and the run loops forever until
it times out. The fix is the vplat runtime
(`build/runtime/libandes_sim_runtime.a`, sources in `runtime/`, link with
`-B build/runtime -specs=andes-sim.specs`): it routes stdio to UART2, exit to
SimControl, and file io to HTIF -- MMIO devices both engines model -- so
`printf` / `exit` / `fopen` inside the ROI work on fast, cycle, AND hybrid
(USER_GUIDE section 5; smoke tests in `tests/vplat/`). Every C fixture in the
repo links it; nothing in-tree uses `-lgloss_vh`. The limitation survives
only for EXTERNAL binaries linked against a semihosting libgloss: keep their
I/O in phase 1 (the QEMU leg, before the ROI), or relink with vplat.

### L6. Whole-program (S/U-mode) privilege  (F-T2.1) -- RESOLVED

Was: a kernel/Linux-style workload in S- or U-mode at the trigger was
silently measured in M-mode (both sides hardcoded `priv = 3`; DCSR.prv was
never written). Now the privilege round-trips: the plugin drains the gdbstub
`priv` virtual register, `ResumeDriver` read-modify-writes `dcsr.prv` before
`dret` and reads it back (an RTL without S/U WARL-pins the field and the
resume aborts with a "pick an S/U-capable engine" error rather than measuring
the wrong privilege; reserved `priv=2` is rejected up front), for S/U states
the producer's PMP block is mirrored first (L2 slice), and `StateDrain` reads
`dcsr.prv` at the exit halt so `--verify` compares it. Residual envelope: one
privilege throughout (no traps/xRET), paging off (L3), S-mode CSRs not
transported. e2e: `rt_priv_smode` / `rt_priv_umode` on the S/U-capable
`ax66_makatau` engine paired with QEMU `-cpu andes-ax66`. The grep below
shows the live privilege drain plus the one remaining static `priv=3` (the
plugin's atexit count record, which has no vCPU context).
!grep -n "priv" verilator/src/hybrid/state_drain.hpp qemu_plugin/hybrid_handoff.c | grep -E "= 3|dcsr|0x3"

### L11. VLEN ceiling  (F-T3.4) -- RESOLVED for the supported range 128..1024

Was: the wire format reserved 64 bytes per vector register (VLEN 512) and the
plugin CLAMPED the drained bytes to that with no warning -- a wider engine
silently lost the upper bytes of every V register. Now
`HYBRID_VLEN_BYTES_MAX = 128` (state version 2) covers VLEN 128..1024; the
plugin REFUSES to drain an over-ceiling vlenb (`hybrid_v_drain_policy`)
instead of clamping, vsim's `load_state` rejects an over-ceiling state file
the same way, and every reader rejects version-1 files loudly. The live width
is the runtime `vlenb`, so one struct layout serves every engine and the legs
never disagree on offsets. Verified per VLEN with `tests/fixtures/rt_c_v_fill.c`
(whole-register fill + in-ROI self-check) and `tests/hybrid/e2e_vlen1024_drain.sh`.
Residual (ROADMAP F-ENG-03): a vsim-side compare of the live hart vlenb vs
`state.vlenb` at resume is still open; no built RTL engine reports VLEN 256 or
1024 today, so those widths are validated on the QEMU side.

### L12. CSR 0x7C0 trigger collision -- RESOLVED by the trigger redesign

The old default trigger matched `csrwi 0x7C0, 0/1`, so a real write to that
CSR would false-trigger a handoff. The default trigger is now the marker HINT
pair `slti x0, x0, 0x5A0/0x5A1` -- rd=x0 makes them architectural NOPs, no
CSR is repurposed, and a compiler never emits them on its own (users get them
from `<andes_sim/ROI.h>`). Binaries you cannot edit use `--trigger pc`.
Where: `qemu_plugin/hybrid_handoff.c` (marker matcher);
`verilator/src/hybrid/csr_trigger.hpp`.

### L13. Marker must be a 32-bit instruction  (B18) -- RESOLVED (exact by construction)

The matcher skips any instruction whose size is not 4 bytes, but the markers
are now `slti x0, x0, imm` and SLTI has no compressed form, so the `sz != 4`
skip is exact rather than an approximation (`hybrid_handoff.c`).

### L16. CSR restore to QEMU2 silently skipped  -- REMOVED

The QEMU2 handback leg restored CSRs by gdbstub name and skipped quietly when
the stub did not advertise one. The leg was deleted (the cycle figure is now
the vsim `mcycle` delta with no handback), so the failure mode no longer
exists.

### L17. gdbstub timeout + racy port pick  -- REMOVED

The handback's fixed 10 s gdbstub timeout and TOCTOU port pick died with the
QEMU2 leg.

### L20. FP rounding mode (fcsr) does not round-trip -- RESOLVED

Was: a workload that set a non-default rounding mode (`frm != RNE`) before the
ROI, or relied on sticky `fflags`, ran the ROI with the reset value because
`fcsr` (which packs `frm[7:5]` and `fflags[4:0]`) was not in
`hybrid_state_v1`. Now `fcsr` round-trips end to end, gated on
`HYBRID_FLAG_FP`: one `uint64` carved from `reserved[]`, drained by the plugin
alongside the FPRs, restored via the abstract-or-PB CSR path under the same
`mstatus.FS` enable, re-read at drain, and compared by `--verify`. Pre-fix
state files read back 0 (the old reset-value behavior), so no version bump.
Proven by `tests/fixtures/rt_c_fcsr.c` and the marker/pc e2e suite. This is
the worked example for the carve-from-`reserved[]` recipe that L21/L23/L24
reused.

### L23. mscratch (M-mode software scratch CSR) did not round-trip -- RESOLVED

`mscratch` (CSR 0x340) is the M-mode software scratch register -- a
side-effect-free read/write CSR, legal inside a trap-free, single-privilege
ROI. It was drained by QEMU1 but never restored into vsim and never re-read
at drain, so a value stashed before the ROI read back as the vsim reset value
(the resume gap) and a value written inside the ROI was dropped from the
drained state (the drain gap); `--verify` could not catch the second because
`state_diff` excluded `mscratch` as a "passthrough CSR", and the repo's guard
(`rt_csr_survival.S`) had gone dead in the 2-phase redesign. This broke a
workload sitting ENTIRELY inside the supposedly-safe envelope, so the
envelope list was incomplete. Now `mscratch` round-trips: restored via the
tolerant CSR write right after `mtvec`, re-read in
`drain_with_passthrough`, and strictly compared by `state_diff` in the hybrid
policy. Guard: `rt_csr_survival.S` revived as a live 2-phase self-check, plus
unit cases in `resume_driver.test.cpp` / `state_drain.test.cpp` /
`state_diff_test.cpp`.

### L24. Writable M-mode trap/interrupt CSRs did not round-trip -- RESOLVED

Same shape as L23, for `mepc`, `mcause`, `mtval`, `mie`, `mip` -- writable
M-mode CSRs that read/write without a trap, interrupt, or paging. They were
drained but never restored and never re-read, so they suffered the same
resume gap + drain gap and `--verify` was blind to them. Now
`ResumeDriver::resume` restores all five via tolerant abstract writes,
`StateDrain::drain_with_passthrough` re-reads all five, and `state_diff`
compares `mepc`/`mcause`/`mtval`/`mie` under the hybrid policy
(`mepc`/`mcause` also lock-step). The exception is `mip`: restored and re-read
but EXCLUDED from `--verify`, because its pending bits (MTIP/MEIP/MSIP) are
hardware/platform-driven and the timer bit advances differently in the
functional vs cycle clocks, so comparing it would false-positive. On the
M-only default engine the `mip` restore is a no-op; it does real work on
S-capable engines. `medeleg`/`mideleg`/`satp` stay unrestored (S-mode CSRs the
default engine lacks; see L3/L4). This is what made L4 stop being "trap state
is lost".

### L26. V transport scratch moved above the program's RAM -- RESOLVED

Was: the V-register transport staged 32 vector registers through a FIXED guest
address `0x00FF0000` (15 MiB), INSIDE the program's RAM. On every resume on a
V-capable core (the V flag is set from register ADVERTISEMENT, not use, so even
a program issuing no V instruction triggered it) `ResumeDriver` wrote the
drained V bytes there, silently clobbering any program data at that address.
Now the scratch is the TOP page of the mapped RAM span,
`v_scratch_gpa(ram_base, ram_size) = ram_base + ram_size -
HYBRID_V_SCRATCH_BYTES`; the driver maps one page MORE than `--mem-size`
(`shm.cpp`), so the scratch sits just above the program's declared RAM where
no layout can reach it, and a load-time guard (`elf_load_top` + `cmd_run.cpp`)
rejects an ELF whose static image extends into the reserved page.
`ResumeDriver`/`StateDrain` take the GPA as a required-when-V argument and
throw if it is unset (no silent transport through a bogus address). Users see
nothing change -- they get their full `--mem-size`; the reservation is one
hidden page on top. `break_vscratch.S` (sentinel at the old 0x00FF0000) now
PASSES, and `break_vscratch_top.S` (sentinel at the program's last page)
PASSES, proving the scratch sits above program RAM.

## Commercial product quality rating

Honest scorecard for "is this a shippable commercial product today?". Rated
against industry baselines (Synopsys VCS, Cadence Xcelium, gem5 + functional
warmup) for a CPU vendor's hybrid-sim offering.

**Overall: 4/10 as a shippable commercial product. ~7/10 as an internal /
research tool inside its narrow design envelope.**

### Axis breakdown

| Axis                                  | Score | Note |
|---------------------------------------|-------|------|
| Architecture clarity                  | 8/10  | Two-phase handoff is clean; shared ABI is a single header. |
| Engineering discipline                | 7/10  | TDD gate, doctest, parallel CI, a candid limitations doc. |
| State coverage (correctness surface)  | 4/10  | 26 documented limitations (11 resolved/removed); 13 scalar CSRs round-trip into vsim, plus privilege, the V CSRs, and PMP for S/U. |
| Generality of workload                | 2/10  | ROI must be single-privilege (M/S/U), effectively trap-free, paging-off (L2-L5). |
| ISA completeness                      | 3/10  | S/U mode and fcsr now transport; still no HPM, zero Andes vendor CSRs beyond the cache/misc pair (vendor IS Andes). |
| Wire-format extensibility             | 4/10  | v1 only; growth happens by carving `reserved[192]` ad-hoc. No v2 path. |
| Robustness / errors                   | 5/10  | `cmderr` is cleared and swallowed; only a private diagnostic side channel. |
| Docs / onboarding                     | 7/10  | `CLAUDE.md`, `USER_GUIDE.md`, and this notebook are unusually honest. |
| Test fixtures                         | 6/10  | Solid asm + C-runtime e2e; FP-rounding and S/U-privilege covered; LR/SC and time-variant-CSR break fixtures; still no in-ROI trap-fault fixture. |
| Portability                           | 4/10  | x86-64 host + little-endian assumed (L18); pinned Andes toolchain; podman-only vsim build. |

### What blocks commercial shipping

1. **Silent correctness gaps.** `cmderr` is W1C-cleared, so a partial CSR
   restore is observable only through a private counter
   (`resume_driver.hpp`, `cmderr_clear_count()`).
2. **ROI envelope is too narrow.** S/U privilege transports now (on an
   S/U-capable engine), but "no paging, no delegation, effectively no traps,
   no semihosting inside the window" (L2-L5) still rules out every real
   OS-bearing benchmark -- SPEC under Linux, any driver code, anything with
   page faults. The vplat runtime covers bare-metal I/O only.
3. **No Andes vendor CSRs beyond the cache/misc pair.** For an Andes product,
   shipping near-zero `mmsc_cfg / mxstatus / ...` transport (L21) is a
   credibility hit and an accuracy hazard -- prefetcher and predictor controls
   shape the cycle count.
4. **13 scalar CSRs restored into vsim** (`mstatus, mtvec, mscratch, mepc,
   mcause, mtval, mie, mip, mcycle, minstret, fcsr, mcache_ctl, mmisc_ctl`),
   plus `dcsr.prv` and -- for S/U handoffs -- the PMP block. `satp` and
   `medeleg`/`mideleg` (and PMP on M-mode handoffs) are drained but never
   written back. Any future need for paging or S-mode delegation inside the
   ROI needs `resume_driver` extended.
5. **Wire format is v1-locked with ad-hoc growth.** Each new field steals
   from `reserved[]` (warmup metadata, fcsr, the cache pair). No deprecation
   path, no feature bits beyond the three `HYBRID_FLAG_*` bits.
6. **Build/test infrastructure is single-host.** Podman-required vsim build,
   a practical `JOBS=8` ceiling on 128-core hosts, `/dev/shm`-backed fixtures
   -- fine for a lab, painful for a commercial CI matrix.

### What it does well (the 7/10 internal-tool score)

- Two-phase handoff is a clear, documented contract.
- `state_abi.h` plus `static_assert`s pin layout -- good ABI hygiene.
- The team writes down what does NOT work (this notebook) instead of hiding
  it. Commercially that is the release-blocker checklist; internally it is
  exemplary.
- SimPoint integration for whole-program cycle estimation (L14) is a real
  differentiator over a pure functional sim.

### Bottom line

Ship-grade architecture, research-grade coverage. For commercial release you
need: a v2 wire format with feature bits and a deprecation path; paging +
delegation supported inside the ROI (close L3, L4); Andes vendor CSR transport
(close L21); a proper error policy instead of `cmderr` swallowing; and the
existing `--verify`/`--cosim` oracle (L15) extended to icount/simpoint and
wired into CI. Rough effort: 6-9 months of focused hardening, not weeks.

# Bare-Metal Profiling - Limitations

What the hybrid simulator cannot do when you profile a **bare-metal** program:
one standalone application, single privilege (M-mode), **no OS / no Linux
kernel**, and **no co-simulation**.

This is a focused subset of `andes_sim_limitations.ipynb`. That master doc
lists every limitation and owns the `L`-ids; this notebook keeps only the ones
a bare-metal user actually hits, written as a short "do / do not" tutorial.
For anything outside this use case (OS / Linux workloads, S-mode paging,
lock-step co-sim) read the master doc.

Two kinds of entry below:

- **Hard limit** - the run hangs, crashes, or returns a wrong result.
- **Accuracy caveat** - the run finishes, but the cycle number can mislead.

Every claim is backed by a cell that runs a real command against this repo.
""")

# 1 -- setup md
md(r"""
## Setup

Already built: the driver (`build/andes-sim`), the vsim engine, and the test
fixtures (`tests/fixtures/*.elf`). The `break_*` fixtures misbehave on purpose
and are built individually. If anything is missing, run `source ./setup.sh`
from the repo root.
""")

from pathlib import Path
root = next(str(d) for d in (Path.cwd(), *Path.cwd().parents)
            if (d / "build" / "andes-sim").exists())
os.chdir(root)
os.environ["PATH"] = f"{root}/build:" + os.environ["PATH"]
print("working dir:", root)
""", output="working dir: /home/nick/work/hybrid_sim")

# 3 -- the one rule
md(r"""
## The one rule: keep the measured window simple

Profiling measures one region of your program - the **ROI**, between the entry
and exit triggers. When the run hands that region to the cycle-accurate vsim
engine, only part of the CPU state crosses the boundary. So the measured region
MUST stay inside this envelope:

- **One privilege level** throughout (bare metal = M-mode). No privilege change
  inside the ROI.
- **No paging** (`satp = 0`). Bare metal already runs in bare address mode, so
  this is free - just do not turn paging on.
- **No held atomic** (`lr`/`sc`) reservation across the entry trigger.
- **Effectively trap-free.** A simple synchronous M-mode trap + handler is OK
  (shown below); delegation and page faults are not.
- **No asynchronous interrupts** inside the window.
- **I/O only through the vplat runtime** (UART2 + SimControl). No semihosting.

Step outside the envelope and the result is silently wrong or the run hangs.
Each item below is one consequence of this rule.
""")

## I/O: link the vplat runtime, never semihosting  (L1)

A bare-metal program still needs `printf` / `exit` / file I/O. Use the **vplat
runtime**, which routes them to MMIO devices both engines model (stdio ->
UART2, exit -> SimControl, files -> HTIF). Link it with
`-B build/runtime -specs=andes-sim.specs`; every C fixture in this repo does.

Do NOT link a semihosting libgloss (`-lgloss_vh`). vsim has no semihosting
handler, so the semihosting `ebreak` traps, the handler calls `_exit` (another
`ebreak`), and the run loops forever until it times out.

the cycle-accurate vsim leg - and still yields a clean `window_cycles`.
""")

# Bare-Metal Profiling - Limitations

What the hybrid simulator cannot do when you profile a **bare-metal** program:
one standalone application, single privilege (M-mode), **no OS / no Linux
kernel**, and **no co-simulation**.

This is a focused subset of `andes_sim_limitations.ipynb`. That master doc
lists every limitation and owns the `L`-ids; this notebook keeps only the ones
a bare-metal user actually hits, written as a short "do / do not" tutorial.
For anything outside this use case (OS / Linux workloads, S-mode paging,
lock-step co-sim) read the master doc.

Two kinds of entry below:

- **Hard limit** - the run hangs, crashes, or returns a wrong result.
- **Accuracy caveat** - the run finishes, but the cycle number can mislead.

Every claim is backed by a cell that runs a real command against this repo.

## Setup

Already built: the driver (`build/andes-sim`), the vsim engine, and the test
fixtures (`tests/fixtures/*.elf`). The `break_*` fixtures misbehave on purpose
and are built individually. If anything is missing, run `source ./setup.sh`
from the repo root.

## The one rule: keep the measured window simple

Profiling measures one region of your program - the **ROI**, between the entry
and exit triggers. When the run hands that region to the cycle-accurate vsim
engine, only part of the CPU state crosses the boundary. So the measured region
MUST stay inside this envelope:

- **One privilege level** throughout (bare metal = M-mode). No privilege change
  inside the ROI.
- **No paging** (`satp = 0`). Bare metal already runs in bare address mode, so
  this is free - just do not turn paging on.
- **No held atomic** (`lr`/`sc`) reservation across the entry trigger.
- **Effectively trap-free.** A simple synchronous M-mode trap + handler is OK
  (shown below); delegation and page faults are not.
- **No asynchronous interrupts** inside the window.
- **I/O only through the vplat runtime** (UART2 + SimControl). No semihosting.

Step outside the envelope and the result is silently wrong or the run hangs.
Each item below is one consequence of this rule.

## I/O: link the vplat runtime, never semihosting  (L1)

A bare-metal program still needs `printf` / `exit` / file I/O. Use the **vplat
runtime**, which routes them to MMIO devices both engines model (stdio ->
UART2, exit -> SimControl, files -> HTIF). Link it with
`-B build/runtime -specs=andes-sim.specs`; every C fixture in this repo does.

Do NOT link a semihosting libgloss (`-lgloss_vh`). vsim has no semihosting
handler, so the semihosting `ebreak` traps, the handler calls `_exit` (another
`ebreak`), and the run loops forever until it times out.

Below, `vplat_hello.elf` prints from INSIDE the measured window - serviced by
the cycle-accurate vsim leg - and still yields a clean `window_cycles`.
